paragraphs: Rabbi Yaakov bar Ami or Imi.

In Sanhedrin 20b, Rabbi Yaakov bar Ami says, “A bed whose canopy poles protrude—stand it upright, and that suffices.” Hyman reports the reading bar Acha in Nedarim 56a; see that entry. At the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, chapter 6, Rabbi Yaakov bar Ami reports Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.

notes.text: The supplied גרם בר אחא is read contextually as a variant reading, bar Acha, rather than as a person named Garam bar Acha.
